I read that compared to the United Kingdom's donations to that United Nations Fund, the Gates Foundation was giving 14 times as much money as the whole United Kingdom. They're pouring money into changing the economy, focusing on Africa, privatizing the economy, farming, and the health care system.

**John Barkhausen:** I did read something about the WHO never used to take money from private persons or organizations before, but now they are. Does that mean that basically they're open to funding from the pharmaceuticals as well as NGOs?

**Dr. Raymond Peat:** Yeah, I think the pharmaceuticals are probably the biggest source of money.

**John Barkhausen:** Do you have any specific worries about that?

**Dr. Raymond Peat:** The drug companies would be happy if everyone took a flu vaccine. But the trouble is, the flu vaccines contain multiple antigens besides influenza. Or if they get a coronavirus antigen, they contain adjuvants and junk antigens, such as the cells they were using in their culture process. So it's a very complex and highly inflammatory material that they use just to promote the immune reaction.

The trouble is that the viruses mutate so quickly. After one, two, or three years, they are very likely to have disappeared and might never come back. But it takes a year and a half or two, typically, to make a vaccine. In 1975 and 1976, the CDC's man in charge of overseeing flu vaccines kept telling his bosses that it was futile to try to get a vaccine in time to catch these rapidly mutating viruses. They ignored him and went on with the program. Finally, he went on television and got fired for it. But he exposed the basically fraudulent idea that you could have an effective and harmless flu vaccine.

**John Barkhausen:** Is there any way to judge the efficacy of a flu shot?

**Dr. Raymond Peat:** They aim to get an antibody produced in first the animals and then the people. The trouble is that the antibodies have some generality and overlap, but they are fairly specific for a particular strain. So they're not much good for the next strain that comes in around the time that the flu vaccine becomes available.

The real part of the immune system—which is really prior to the vaccines and is, I think, a more important part—is the so-called innate immune system. It has been known for at least 20 or 30 years to be trainable or educable, the same way the adaptive antibody system is. The fundamental whole-body processes that catch viruses in many ways and reduce the harm they do just aren't attended to. The vaccine companies can demonstrate that they're producing antibodies, but they can't clearly show what's happening in the innate system because it involves changes in the whole body. This starts with, for example, the surfactant protein in the air sacs of the lungs, the nature of the composition of the mucus, and the surface of the cells.

**John Barkhausen:** And those are all surfaces where a surfactant is supposed to be present to protect you?

**Dr. Raymond Peat:** Yeah. Healthy mucus is a very powerful protector, especially if the mucus is being swept constantly out of your lungs. Once in the cell, there are many layers of other innate protectors. Since the coronavirus in particular is known to activate all of the inflammatory processes—including tending to stop the flow of mucus out of your tubes and changing the circulatory pattern, releasing histamine, serotonin, angiotensin—everything that is harmful is activated by these infectious things.

**John Barkhausen:** Maybe we could talk about how, as a country, we can move forward and approach this problem rationally.

**Dr. Raymond Peat:** I think that's the important thing, because they're deliberately getting people scared so that they will be ready to get vaccinated next season. Our whole generation, going back at least 50 years, has been heavily indoctrinated to go to the doctor. People are trained to think of the medical profession as protective, but there's really no objective evidence that that protects against anything.

In fact, when you look at the studies that try to be objective, there are two publications I know that looked at hospital deaths alone. One group said at least 220,000 deaths are caused by accidents caused by the medical staff. Another group said 440,000 deaths per year are caused by medical mistakes. Those numbers already put deaths caused by medical mistakes in third place behind heart disease and cancer deaths. And that wasn't including hospital-acquired infections, which amount to around 100,000 deaths per year.

Since there's nothing safe and effective against the virus, people are going into the hospitals with very little examination and they are putting them on ventilators. One of the common practices when people come in with respiratory infections, even before they go on a ventilator, is to give them aerosolized antivirals such as ribavirin, even though there's no published evidence showing that reduces mortality. Since they know it works in vitro—it'll reduce the virus in cells in a culture dish—but there's no proven evidence that it protects the person against the virus in the living state.

**John Barkhausen:** Is this antivirals you mean?

**Dr. Raymond Peat:** Yeah. Hydroxychloroquine is classified as an antimalarial and anti-inflammatory for rheumatoid arthritis. But these nucleoside analogs or the hydroxychloroquine categories are all recognized as hazardous, mutagenic, possibly carcinogenic drugs. They damage the RNA or DNA of the virus, but they also damage the human DNA and RNA.

The ventilation itself, if they have to stick a tube down your windpipe, tends to activate inflammation just by the mechanical damage it does. They are typically using 40% to 60% oxygen supplement. Sometimes it's just air, but if you speed the respiration with just ordinary air, and especially if you double or triple the amount of oxygen, you're necessarily going to reduce the amount of carbon dioxide in their lungs and bloodstream. Carbon dioxide is a major anti-inflammatory defense against the damage that the viruses are doing. Scientifically, there's a lot of evidence to show that what they're doing very quickly when someone gets to the hospital panicked over the coronavirus is very, very dangerous.

**John Barkhausen:** If you do have some respiratory problem and you're having trouble getting enough oxygen, it seems like that would naturally increase your CO2 as a response to that.

**Dr. Raymond Peat:** If they would more generally use Carbogen, which is 5% carbon dioxide added to oxygen, that will give you more oxygen actually than just hyperventilating a person. The carbon dioxide is anti-inflammatory and has many pro-respiratory effects. It helps to deliver the oxygen, moving it from the blood into the energy-producing cells. And it opens up capillaries that have been constricted by such things as angiotensin produced by infection.

**John Barkhausen:** So if you wanted to instruct somebody how to do it, you'd say if you had to do the ventilator, you'd do 35% oxygen and 5% CO2?

**Dr. Raymond Peat:** I think even 1% CO2 would be a big help.

**John Barkhausen:** I was wondering, do masks increase your CO2 levels? I feel like it's like breathing into a bag.

**Dr. Raymond Peat:** Not very much. The carbon dioxide doesn't stay in place.

**John Barkhausen:** That brings me to the subject of anti-inflammatories. I heard a show with an English doctor named John Campbell. He concluded that there's a reason we get a fever and it's important, especially with coronavirus. He quoted some French medical ministers saying that with the fever of coronavirus, it can cause a lot of negative complications if you use anti-inflammatories of any kind. What is your opinion about that?

**Dr. Raymond Peat:** I saw that, but I also saw his video on vitamin D. The vitamin D talk is very good, and what vitamin D is doing is profoundly anti-inflammatory. But he recommends vitamin D, aspirin, vitamin B1, and progesterone. Their benefit is in this situation largely by lowering the angiotensin receptor, a very central basic thing in anti-inflammatory protection. So vitamin D is one of our central anti-inflammatory things and very protective against all kinds of viral infections.

**John Barkhausen:** Going back to John Campbell talking about fever being important and not getting in the way of the fever's work to kill off the coronavirus, do you feel like aspirin would interfere with the fever?

**Dr. Raymond Peat:** Aspirin can often increase your thyroid function and cell respiration so much that it doesn't affect your fever, but it can lower the *need* for a fever. Since angiotensin overproduction is a basic harm factor of any infection, you're stopping the mechanism of the harm. That is what is lowering the fever. It isn't just mechanically turning off heat production. It actually increases oxidative metabolism and, at least temporarily, will increase thyroid function. So when it reduces a fever, I think it's most often because it's remedying the thing that is causing the fever.

**John Barkhausen:** Does the fever actually kill the virus?

**Dr. Raymond Peat:** It activates various parts of your immune reaction. The ability to produce antibodies, for example, is increased with fever. And white blood cells can eat faster at a higher temperature. So in general, your resistance is increased with the fever.

**John Barkhausen:** Is there anything we didn't cover that you wanted to?

**Dr. Raymond Peat:** A lot of places are warning about anti-inflammatory drugs. They're extending it to aspirin. They're generally getting confused, thinking that the ACE2 enzyme—which is the target of the coronavirus—shouldn't be increased because it would increase the chance of catching the coronavirus. There was an article in *The Lancet* that said basically the same thing: stop taking anti-inflammatories because they'll increase your ACE2 enzyme and make a bigger target. But there had already been half a dozen very clear papers saying that the virus *decreases* your ACE2 enzyme, increasing the pro-inflammatory angiotensin production. So what you need to do is get your ACE2 back in production to destroy the inflammatory mediator.

**John Barkhausen:** I was reading an opinion piece by Scott Atlas working off the epidemiological analysis by Dr. John Ioannidis. He was saying it doesn't make much sense to lock everybody up forever. He thought it would make much more sense to only try to isolate those who are most vulnerable and let the rest of the population build up immunity.

**Dr. Raymond Peat:** That's very reasonable. Sweden has basically done nothing resembling the United States program. The government there so far has told old people and sick people to stay home, and everyone to wash their hands and basically just behave sensibly, not shutting down businesses.

**John Barkhausen:** Just to sum up, Ray, if you wouldn't mind going over again all the things one can do to keep themselves healthy and keep an innate immune system working. Sleep would be one of those, isn't it?

**Dr. Raymond Peat:** Yeah. And a good diet is necessary for sleep. Vitamin D and the associated calcium work together. Vitamin D is anti-inflammatory, but it works by lowering parathyroid hormone. It can't do that if your phosphate intake is very high relative to calcium. So cutting down on your beans, nuts, meat, and fish, and increasing cooked green leaves, cheese, and milk will improve the function of the anti-inflammatory, anti-infective vitamin D, lowering the parathyroid hormone and all of the associated pro-inflammatory things that it does.

**John Barkhausen:** Well, that sounds good. Let's see if we can work on that. Dr. Raymond Peat, thanks so much for being on the show today and I really appreciate getting your analysis.

**Dr. Raymond Peat:** Okay. Thanks.

**Host:** It might be a wonderful world for you if you listen to our guest, Dr. Raymond Peat. Aloha, Dr. Peat, how are you today?

**Dr. Raymond Peat:** Hello. Very good.

**Host:** We're thrilled to have you on our show. All week long, Karen and I have been telling people in our store that you're going to be our guest. Everybody loves your books. I understand you started working with hormones and progesterone back in 1968. I'm curious, what caused you to get into this field?

**Dr. Raymond Peat:** I had been teaching linguistics and painting alternately, but I had been interested in science from childhood. I saw medical "science" going off in very perverse directions through the 1950s. I didn't think of going to university graduate school in biology because my bad experience in high school biology—with very retarded textbooks—made me think there wasn't much science in the biological field. Finally, I decided that I needed to use laboratory instruments that were too expensive to get myself. So, I enrolled in graduate school and figured that just by not arguing with the teachers, I could get through the program and use the lab, which I did.

**Karen:** Your insight always amazes me because I'm one of those gullible believers. When I am told that I should take estrogen because I'm aging, I believed it. In fact, I was writing a dissertation on the positive benefits of estrogen until I met you. It blew all that stuff right out of the water. I look back at how gullible I was and how easily people are misled into believing what the pharmaceutical industries want them to believe.

**Dr. Raymond Peat:** Advertising is very powerful. A group of 13 estrogen companies got together in 1942 when it was already known that estrogen caused miscarriages, sterility, cancer, seizures, and so on. But they had a product and they wanted to sell it as the "female hormone," even though it's also a male hormone. They got together and, with advertising and political pressure, convinced the FDA to approve the use of estrogen to prevent miscarriages—which it actually caused. By advertising, they got the public interested in estrogen as an anti-aging hormone. So, it started really with a definite conspiracy of 13 companies in 1942.

**Karen:** It has continued to this day, even with well-meaning individuals like Suzanne Somers, who advocates the use of bioidentical hormones. She always throws large amounts of estrogen into the equation, including estriol. Would you mind talking about that?

**Dr. Raymond Peat:** The body has many protective systems for inactivating the strong estrogen, estradiol. It has enzymes to oxidize it in different ways. By oxidizing it to estriol or estrone, it reduces the estrogen-like activity. It also has several other systems for destroying estrogen efficiently. If your metabolism is working very well, estrogen should be totally eliminated about 12 hours following ovulation and implantation. It should be disposed of thoroughly within a few days of ovulation.

**Host:** I'm amazed that having worked in the natural foods industry for 42 years, when I read my trade magazines, I'm still seeing advertisements for estrogen-based products. It's not only in the pharmaceutical industry; it's in the natural foods industry.

**Karen:** But it's not that estrogen is bad, right? It's that it needs to be in a certain ratio.

**Dr. Raymond Peat:** I've been thinking of how common estrogen is throughout the universe. Anytime an organism is injured, it produces estrogen, which stimulates growth and repair. But an even more common biological material is ATP, the so-called energy molecule. Anytime we're injured, or even when a cell is slightly stressed, it loses some of its ATP, which acts as a signal to other cells to repair the damage. When a lizard is attacked and drops its tail, it's probably a surge of ATP that cuts the tail off. ATP forms to make a blister, dissolving the tissue between the layers of skin so that fluid flows in. ATP, our most life-supporting basic molecule, has these potentially deadly, destructive effects—cutting off and dissolving tissue so that repair can take place.

Estrogen is just supposed to be biologically active as an excitant at an early stage of injury. For example, it slightly inflames the uterus to cause the growth of cells, preparing a place for the embryo to implant. But if the estrogen stays present too long, it kills the embryo by over-exciting the surrounding cells.

In the 1950s, my thesis advisor, Soderwall, demonstrated that by giving an estrogen supplement to a pregnant animal the day that it becomes pregnant, you can prevent implantation by a small amount, such as is used in birth control pills. That's how they work: by a quick abortion actually, rather than preventing conception. He found that on the second, third, or fourth days following implantation, if you gave just slightly larger amounts of estrogen all the way up until delivery, you could kill the embryo or the fetus, despite adjusting the dose of estrogen to counteract the increasing progesterone. So at any stage, estrogen produces abortion when it is out of balance with progesterone.

**Karen:** If a woman is pregnant and the progesterone levels don't increase?

**Dr. Raymond Peat:** When a woman has a sluggish liver or low thyroid, so that her estrogen is chronically too high or her progesterone is chronically low, she will often bleed every month, several months into the pregnancy, as if she were menstruating. During any of those cyclic surges of estrogen, miscarriages are most likely to happen.

**Karen:** How would this affect the sexual persuasion of the child should that pregnancy make it all the way to the end? How would being bathed in a more highly estrogenic environment affect the child?

**Dr. Raymond Peat:** It damages sexual differentiation. There is some research that prenatal stress causes an intersexual differentiation.

**Karen:** What does that mean exactly?

**Dr. Raymond Peat:** Not definitely either one.

**Karen:** How would that show up with sexual organs? Does that mean you would have hermaphroditism?

**Dr. Raymond Peat:** The main thing is that the male has smaller genitals, and the distance between the genitals and the anus is decreased in proportion to the estrogen exposure.
